scope: Read-only bounded audit of all108 poem occurrences and all5778 pairs in both existing annotated-pronunciation and dictionary-union modes, plus the five original E63 displayed matches. No repository or Site edits and no model training.

homeoteleuton.core: Similar audible word endings in adjacent or parallel positions.

homoioptoton.core: Historically a grammatical/case-ending figure; English adaptations must declare which inflectional features count.

existing_implementation.E63: Native last nucleus+coda+prominence agreement AND declared morphological-affix string agreement AND different words. Pair adapter removes line-final placement, not morphology.
existing_implementation.known_native_fault: relations.py:8450-8478 already documents spurious inflectional segmentation (flatter/matter) and empty-affix equality (day/May). It was removed from validated findings (8515-8517).
existing_implementation.H1: test_homeoteleuton.py documents a same-spelled-rime writing-quality rule. H1 is spelling evidence, not an independent validated literary-figure definition.
existing_implementation.diagnosis: Both definition scope and resource implementation: E63 conflates homeoteleuton with a morphology-dependent subtype, and the suffix guesser does not identify context-sensitive morphemes; the poem adapter then drops native placement.

old_five_decisions.action: Preserve actual E18 sound relation; retire authoritative E63 morphology claim.
Preserve actual E18 sound relation; do not strip -ing mechanically.
Preserve actual E18 sound relation and optional sourced derivation note; no automatic complete-figure label.

sound_predicate.expression: ending(a) == ending(b), where ending is nonempty final nucleus plus complete final coda
sound_predicate.stress_policy: No stress-equality gate for broad sound candidates; retain lexical stress values and both-weak flags. Weak final matches may overlap E18. A stricter same-stress view has124 distinct-word pairs.
sound_predicate.identity_policy: Keep repeated words with a repeated_word flag so overlap with repetition is observable; distinct-word counts are also reported.
sound_predicate.vowel_policy: Reuse selected annotation and declared normalization: schwa remains AH0; declared pre-R vowel normalization is retained. No spelling-based sound identity.
sound_predicate.minimum_extent: A vowel plus all following consonants, not merely any shared final consonant. Open-syllable endings may therefore match one vowel.
sound_predicate.limitations: Exact final-rime equality is a deliberately declared operational subset of similarity, not an exhaustive universal literary definition. Its final-nucleus minimum will not recognize a bare shared plural /z/ unless the preceding rime also agrees.

position_notes.status: depends on the selected /ði/ pronunciation; formal recurrence does not prove deliberate artistic emphasis
adjective slots in coordinated noun phrases; shared weak /i/; no common grammatical inflection inferred
broad homeoteleuton view overlaps the already-observed rhyme families; repeated sleep separately flagged

sound_predicate.unpositioned_policy: Retain nonlocal ending matches as sound evidence; do not silently promote each to a complete rhetorical figure.
sound_predicate.scope_note: The exploratory sound-only list is intentionally broader than the active E63 rule; integration_choice gives the active positional rule and both reading modes.

grammatical_predicate.expression: Both tokens have verified nonempty inflections with equal grammatical feature and same morpheme identity. Surface allomorph equality and adjacent/parallel placement are separate fields.
grammatical_predicate.feature_not_letters: Noun Number=Plural is different from Verb Person=3 Number=Sing Tense=Pres even when both end in spelled -s and pronounced /z/.
grammatical_predicate.annotation_scope: Poem-specific contextual grammar, manually checked; executable comparisons over these annotations, not a claim of a general automatic morphological parser.

singletons_not_recurrence.frozen48: past-participial adjective; no other same-feature suffix match

grammatical_predicate.display_caution: The two promises/miles relationships support parallel shared English plural inflection. Call them an English grammatical-ending interpretation if connecting them to homoioptoton; do not claim classical case-ending identity or force them into the chosen final-rime predicate.

negative_controls.reason: a shared stem is not shared final rime
lexical possessive form is not plural -s
same surface /z/ serves different grammatical features
sound’s means sound is here; the contraction is not a plural suffix
noun evening is not the present participle of even in this context
shared derivation is not grammatical inflection
both adjectives is insufficient to posit the same inflection
absence of any affix on both sides never counts as shared morphology

recommendation: Preserve the original5 E63 results in the audit and their valid sound relations. Replace authoritative E63 figure labeling with explicit sound-ending and placement evidence; keep grammatical-inflection evidence separately named. Label H1 as spelling evidence rather than treating a writing-quality ban as an exhaustive rhetorical definition.

sources.supports: Silva Rhetoricae: similar endings in adjacent or parallel words; grammatical suffix identity is not required.
Silva Rhetoricae: similar case endings in adjacent/parallel positions; notes historical overlap with homoioteleuton. This audit does not import classical case morphology into English.
University of Glasgow: distinguishes derivation from grammatical inflection; noun plural and verb third-person singular are separate inflection categories.
Broeders and Gussenhoven: English plural allomorphs /s/, /z/, /ɪz/; same surface allomorphs also occur in third-person singular and genitive, without making their grammatical meanings identical.
His is possessive determiner/pronoun, the possessive form of he; the suffix heuristic hi + -s does not recover its grammatical identity.
Evening denotes the time-of-day noun used in this poem, not a present participle of the verb even.
Only has historical adjectival -ly derivation; the poem uses the sole/exclusive modifier.
Lovely is an adjective with historical love + -ly derivation; no shared grammatical inflection follows merely from this ending.
Woods in the woodland sense is a plural noun, including the plural agreement shown by the poem itself.
Easy is an adjective; this dictionary gives a French participial origin, so this audit does not infer a common productive English suffix merely from its final letter y.
Downy is an adjective formed with derivational -y; derivation is not plural/tense/degree inflection.

integration_choice.rule_source: Explicit adaptation of broad English word-ending definition S1; replaces the native suffix heuristic in this poem only.
integration_choice.expression: same final nucleus and complete coda AND (same-line adjacent OR verse-line-final OR evidenced easy/downy parallel adjective slots OR aligned word slots in the repeated final line)
integration_choice.same_word_policy: Preserve identical-word matches when a declared position scope holds; seven final-line slot pairs overlap exact repetition. Sleep101/sleep108 also occupies line ends and is counted once.
integration_choice.weak_form_policy: The70/only71 is a formal sound-ending candidate for selected /ði/; the alternative /ðə/ does not support that edge. This is pronunciation evidence, not an inferred artistic intention.
integration_choice.grammatical_output: Contextual evidence only; not an additional inflated pair category.

position_flags.P: parallel adjectives: easy wind and downy flake
position_flags.R: aligned word slots in the exactly repeated final line

integration_choice.witness_note: Both modes have exactly the same34 positive endpoints. Annotated mode31 unique interned witnesses; dictionary union38. All whole pronunciation combinations checked; no mixing phones across readings.
integration_choice.label_scope_warning: This exact-match operationalization is a declared subset of similarity, not a claim to exhaust every literary use of the term or all possible semantic parallelism.
